title: NUMA & CUDA pinning — night shift scratchpad
content:
2026-03-10 22:10 - context
Summary: saw recurring p99 latency spikes (~600ms -> 1.2s) on node-sapphire-02 during low QPS (10 rps), staggered across models that use mixed-precision kernels. No OOMs, but CPU sys% and iowait jump before token generation stalls.

Quick hypothesis thread:
- NUMA misbinding: python worker threads allocating host-side buffers on the wrong NUMA node while CUDA kernels run on another. Leads to cross-node DMA and page fault churn when building KV cache.
- CUDA stream contention + pinned-memory fragmentation: large pinned allocations are being freed/rewritten in tight loops; cudaHostAlloc/cudaFree path might be causing CPU-side stalls.
- Scheduler preemption: GOMP/OpenMP threads from fused ops occasionally migrate and steal CPU from the inference threads.

What I observed (notes):
- spike pattern: starts with a soft preemption/cpu steal (top shows few python pids in D state for ~50-200ms), then cuda kernel queue depth drops and host copy (H2D) latency jumps.
- dmesg had a couple of "Remote TLB flush" and occasional "CPU stall" messages around 21:44.
- NVidia-smi shows tiny spike in GPU utilization drop-off concurrently.

Quick commands run tonight (results inline):
- sudo perf top -p <pid> (brief): high in __memcpy_sse2_unaligned and page_fault handling
- sudo numastat -p <pid>: allocations mostly on node 1 while process affinities showed cores pinned to node 0
- strace -f -tt -p <pid> (short): saw repeated futex waits around cudaHostAlloc/free pairs

Fast experiments (A/B) tried:
A) numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 python serve.py --bind-gpu 0
   -> short-term p99 improved by ~150ms for 15 minutes, then regressed (maybe fragmentation build-up)
B) export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 (debug)
   -> made latency worse (expected) but confirmed ordering effect: host copies are blocking on kernel completion in pathological cases
C) GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY=0-7 (limit threads)
   -> reduced jitter; p99 dropped consistently when OpenMP threads limited to non-inference cores

Interim mitigation we can roll quickly:
- Add runtime flag: --numa-sticky (numactl wrapper for inference worker processes) to bind both CPU and memory to the same NUMA node as local GPU.
- Limit OpenMP threads for fused ops in runtime (env var GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY + OMP_NUM_THREADS=2) for the inference container image.
- Add pre-allocation pool for pinned memory on startup to avoid repeated cudaHostAlloc/free churn.

Follow-ups / TODO (timeboxed):
- [ ] Reproduce in lab with identical load generator (2h) — test cross-node allocation patterns and repeatable p99 regression. (owner: Hector)
- [ ] Create benchmark harness that runs long lived allocate/free pinned-memory loop + mixed-precision kernels to surface fragmentation (owner: Mina, 1d)
- [ ] Open kernel-level perf record and capture full trace around the 21:40 window; correlate with dmesg (owner: Ishaan, 0.5d)
- [ ] RFC: runtime flag semantics + safe default for Dedicated customers (owner: me, draft by Mon)
- [ ] Talk to SRE about machine image: ensure default guc or CPU governor not causing preemption spikes (owner: SRE, ticket INF-2431)

Notes for implementation:
- Pinned allocator: keep a single large cudaHostAlloc pool per worker and sub-alloc from it. Use madvise chunking per-NUMA node so host pages are local.
- Watch for fallback when pool exhausted: allocate but log and rate-limit to avoid cascade.
- prefer-cpu-affinity semantics: if GPU local to node X, bind CPU/mem to X; if config ambiguous, fall back to balanced.

Observability changes to add:
- Add metric: host_pinned_alloc_count and host_pinned_free_count per-worker
- Trace: instrument the host copy start/end and attach to request-id so we can correlate per-request stalls
- Alert: new alert when p99 > 2x baseline and host_pinned_alloc_count spikes by > 10x in 5m

Loose notes / questions for tomorrow:
- Is CUDA peer/access pattern causing pagewalks (P2P disabled vs enabled)? try NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 in a canary.
- Do we need to change kernel boot params for hugepages or published kernel patch for remote TLB flush? Might be risky.
- Should we prefer process-level prebinding (numactl) in init system vs letting k8s cpuset do it? Pros/cons: numactl easy but loses k8s awareness.

Relevant logs snippets (copied):
- "21:44:03.512 pid=14236 [python] [futex_wait] 125ms"
- "21:44:03 dmesg: remote TLB flush request from cpu2 to cpu10"

Slack notes to drop into channel (#serving-runtime):
"Heads-up: running NUMA/CUDA pinning experiments on node-sapphire-02 — short-term mitigation is to enable numa-sticky wrapper and limit OMP threads. Will post benchmark + RFC Monday. Ticket INF-2431."

Quick next steps tonight:
- spin up lab node with identical k8s taint; run allocate/free harness for 2h and capture perf; attach to Jira.
- draft runtime flag PR (small wrapper around our entrypoint to call numactl if requested)

If I don't finish: leave the numactl experiment in place but gated behind an env var so we can roll back quickly.

End of notes.
